feedback: This candidate changes one field from the best raced design, iteration 6 (kd 0.9, scored 511.25): controller.kd goes from 0.9 to 1.0. base_speed 1.1, kp 1.6, ki 0, last_direction, the sensor_weights and the iteration 3 to 6 geometry (x -0.06 to +0.06 in 0.03 m steps, y 0.05, sensor_size 0.012) are unchanged. Iteration 6 shows the oval holding 20/20 at 2.00 s with steering_oscillation 0.185, so the straights tolerate the extra damping. Iteration 5 to 6 (kd 0.7 to 0.9) left s-bend finishes at 5/20 and s-bend max_error at about 0.061 m, so the gain per step is shrinking, which is consistent with the rationale. Iteration 3 (kd 0.5) had s-bend steering_oscillation 0.309, so damping has been reducing bend overshoot but its returns are flattening. This is a clean single-variable step and stays within the contract. I approve it because it is a low-risk test of the best design, with one race needed, and its telemetry will show whether kd still helps. Read the next race as follows. If the oval drops below 20/20 or its steering_oscillation rises well above 0.2, return kd to 0.9 and test kp 1.4 at base_speed 1.1 next. If s-bend finishes stay at or near 5/20 with max_error still at or above 0.06 m, kd has reached its useful range and the next lever should be kp 1.4 with kd 0.9. Do not change the geometry: the iteration 2 change to 0.04 m spacing and y 0.07 scored 62.76 with 2.8 line-loss events on the oval.
requested_changes: If the oval falls below 20/20 finishes or steering_oscillation rises well above 0.2 (iteration 6 was 0.185), return controller.kd to 0.9 and test controller.kp at 1.4 with base_speed 1.1, since kd 0.9 kept the oval at 20/20.
